questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to a limited partnership owned entirely by individuals?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A limited partner may not conduct business with the limited partnership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A general partner may not be a limited partner at the same time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A general partner may be a creditor of the limited partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The limited partnership can be formed with limited liability for all partners.

questions.explanation:
Unlike a general partnership, a limited partnership (LP) provides limited liability to its limited partners. An LP must be managed by one or more general partners, who are jointly and severally liable for the LP's obligations. Therefore, an individual serving as a general partner of an LP has unlimited liability ("The limited partnership can be formed with limited liability for all…").

Much like the managers of a corporation, general partners have a fiduciary duty to the LP and the other partners. This means that a general partner cannot:

compete with the LP.

use the LP's business opportunities for personal gain.

have a conflict of interest with the LP.

conduct LP business in a manner that is reckless, grossly or intentionally negligent, or knowingly violates the law.

A general partner can be a creditor of the LP. However, due to the general partner's fiduciary duty the loan terms must be the same or better than what the LP would receive from a third-party lender.

("A limited partner may not conduct business with the limited partnersh…") A limited partner does not have a fiduciary duty to the LP, or to the other partners, and may conduct business with the LP in the same manner as a third party.

("A general partner may not be a limited partner at the same time.") There are no legal restrictions on owning both a general partner interest and limited partner interest in the same LP.
questions.explanationJa: ジェネラル・パートナーはLPに対して受託者責任を負うが、LPに融資して債権者になることはできる。ただし、その融資条件は第三者の貸し手から受けられる条件と同等以上に有利でなければならない。LPは少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーが経営し、その者は無限責任を負うので、全パートナーが有限責任のLPは作れない。リミテッド・パートナーは受託者責任を負わないので第三者と同様にLPと取引でき、同じLPでジェネラル持分とリミテッド持分を併せ持つことも禁止されていない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.1

questions.stem: Peters owned 500 shares of common stock in Kidsmart, Inc. Accordingly, Peters had the right to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Automatically receive a dividend in any quarter in which the corporation made a profit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inspect the corporate records on demand.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vote for the election and removal of the board of directors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Be a member of the board of directors.

questions.explanation:
A corporation is managed by its board of directors (BOD) and corporate officers, not its shareholders. Even though shareholders own the corporation, they do not manage it. However, they have the right to vote on significant matters affecting the corporation, such as the election and removal of BOD members.

A shareholder may be a BOD member, but ownership of shares in a corporation does not give someone the right to serve on the BOD ("Be a member of the board of directors."). A shareholder, like anyone else, must be elected to the BOD at a shareholder meeting.

("Automatically receive a dividend in any quarter in which the corporat…") Shareholders have a right to receive declared dividends. However, they do not have a right to automatically receive dividends whenever the corporation has a profitable quarter. The decision to declare dividends is made by the BOD.

("Inspect the corporate records on demand.") A shareholder's right to inspect the corporation's records is not an absolute, on-demand right that can be exercised at any time. It's a limited right because the time, place, and purpose of the inspection must be reasonable.
questions.explanationJa: 株主は会社を所有するが経営はしない。それでも、取締役の選任・解任など会社の重要事項について議決権を持つ。配当を受けられるのは取締役会が宣言した場合だけであり、四半期に利益が出れば自動的に受け取れるわけではない。帳簿の閲覧権は、時期・場所・目的が合理的でなければならない限定的な権利である。株主であっても取締役になる権利はなく、株主総会で選任される必要がある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.2

questions.stem: Two CPAs organized their business as a general partnership. Which of the following advantages may have played a role in their selection of the general partnership form under the Revised Uniform Partnership Act?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The partnership form of business organization allowed them to form their business without the requirement of filing organizational documents with a government agency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partners' risk of loss from the business is limited to the amount of capital each invested in the business.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The partnership has a perpetual life that is not affected by a partner's expulsion or withdrawal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The partnership can raise capital with sale of common stock.

questions.explanation:
A general partnership is an association between two or more persons or entities to operate a business as co-owners for profit. A general partnership can be created formally (written agreement) or informally (handshake). In either case, the Revised Uniform Partnership Act (RUPA) does not require a general partnership to file a certificate of formation with the partnership's home state. State laws require a more formal creation process for corporations, limited liability companies, and limited partnerships (formation documents, state filing fees).

("The partners' risk of loss from the business is limited to the amount…") General partners have joint and several liability for the contracts and debts made by the partnership with third parties. Therefore, a partner's risk of loss is greater than just the amount of capital contributed to the partnership.

("The partnership has a perpetual life that is not affected by a partne…") Under RUPA, general partnerships have a limited duration. In a two-person partnership, the duration is also uncertain because if one partner withdraws or dies the partnership terminates.

("The partnership can raise capital with sale of common stock.") Corporations can raise capital through the sale of stock; general partnerships do not have stock. Ownership in a general partnership is represented by a capital account maintained in the partnership's accounting records.
questions.explanationJa: 改訂統一パートナーシップ法（RUPA）では、ジェネラル・パートナーシップは書面でも口頭でも成立し、州に設立書類を提出する必要がない。この手軽さが選択理由になりうる。一方、ジェネラル・パートナーは事業の債務に連帯無限責任を負うので、損失が出資額に限定されることはない。存続期間も限られ、2人のパートナーシップでは1人の脱退や死亡で終了する。株式を発行できるのは会社であり、パートナーシップの持分は資本勘定で表される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.3

questions.stem:
Carr, Dunn, Evall, and Farr formed a general partnership. Their written partnership agreement provided that the profits would be divided so that Carr would receive 40%; Dunn, 30%; Evall, 20%; and Farr, 10%. There was no provision for allocating losses. At the end of its first year, the partnership had losses of $275,000. Before losses were allocated, the partners' capital account balances were: Carr, $150,000; Dunn, $110,000; Evall, $85,000; and Farr, $14,000. All partners agreed to contribute cash to restore any deficit capital account balance they may have. Ignore the effects of federal partnership tax law.

After losses were allocated to the partners' capital accounts and all liabilities were paid, and before any deficit capital account balances were restored, the partnership's sole asset was $84,000 in cash. How much would Dunn receive on termination of the partnership?
questions.explanation:
The following four procedures must be performed:

Allocate gains and losses from asset sales based on partner profit and loss percentages.

Partners with a resulting deficit capital account balance contribute cash to restore the balance to $0 (if they have money).

Prorate any unrestored deficit balance among the remaining partners based on their profit and loss percentages. If there are no separately stated loss percentages, use the profit percentages.

Distribute the remaining cash to the partners in the amounts reflected in the final balance of each partner's capital account.

Based on these procedures, the amount of cash distributed to Dunn (and the other partners) is as follows:

Partner | Profit % (a) | Beg cap acct (b) | Loss allocation (c = a × 275,000) | Adj balance (d = b + c) | Deficit partner cash contribution | Final balance and cash (d + e)
Carr | 40% | $150,000 | ($110,000) | $40,000 |  | $40,000
Dunn | 30% | 110,000 | (82,500) | 27,500 |  | 27,500
Evall | 20% | 85,000 | (55,000) | 30,000 |  | 30,000
Farr | 10% | 14,000 | (27,500) | (13,500) | $13,500 | 0
Total | 100% | $359,000 | ($275,000) | $84,000 | $13,500 | $97,500

Dunn will receive a $27,500 cash distribution.

("$0") Farr is the partner who will not receive any cash distribution.

("$23,000") Dunn would receive a distribution of $23,000 if Farr did not restore the $13,500 deficit balance and it was allocated to the remaining partners [ 27,500-30%90%×13,500
questions.explanationJa: 損失の配分割合に定めがないので、利益の割合で損失$275,000を配分する。Carrは$150,000−$110,000＝$40,000、Dunnは$110,000−$82,500＝$27,500、Evallは$85,000−$55,000＝$30,000、Farrは$14,000−$27,500＝−$13,500となる。全員が欠損を補填することに合意しているので、Farrが$13,500を拠出して残高を0にし、現金は$84,000＋$13,500＝$97,500になる。各パートナーは最終資本残高どおりに現金を受け取るので、Dunnの受取額は$27,500である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.4

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of a limited partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All partners have limited liability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited partnerships must have at least one general partner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The death of a limited partner terminates the partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited partnerships are taxed as separate entities for federal tax purposes.

questions.explanation:
Limited partnerships (LPs) are pass-through entities that are not subject to taxation ("Limited partnerships are taxed as separate entities for federal tax p…"). Instead, partners include their shares of partnership income/loss and separately stated items on their own tax returns.

To form an LP, the owners must file a certificate of limited partnership with the appropriate state authority (secretary of state). The LP must have at least one general partner and one limited partner. The general partner is responsible for the management and operations of the partnership and has unlimited liability ("All partners have limited liability."). Limited partners are considered passive investors (like shareholders in a corporation) and have limited liability.

("The death of a limited partner terminates the partnership.") In most cases, the withdrawal of the general partner will terminate an LP. It will continue, however, if allowed by the LP agreement or if all remaining partners agree to do so in writing. The death or withdrawal of a limited partner will not terminate an LP.
questions.explanationJa: LPを設立するには州（州務長官など）にLP設立証明書を提出し、少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーと1人のリミテッド・パートナーが必要である。ジェネラル・パートナーは経営を担い無限責任を負うので、全員が有限責任になることはない。リミテッド・パートナーは受動的な投資家であり、その死亡や脱退でLPは終了しない。また、LPはパススルー事業体であり、連邦税上、独立した課税主体ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.5

questions.stem:
Which of the following facts is (are) generally included in a corporation's articles of incorporation?
Name of registered agent | Number of authorized shares

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
A corporation is formed by filing the articles of incorporation with the appropriate state agency (secretary of state). The corporation is formally created when the state accepts (approves) the articles. Generally, the articles must include the following:

Name: This is the corporation's proposed The state may reject the name if it is already being used by another business entity.

Nature and purpose: This is a description of the corporation's planned business (clothing manufacturer). However, it often includes broader language ("and any other lawful activity") so the corporation can pursue other business opportunities.

Term: The corporation's life can be set for a limited or indefinite duration.

Incorporators: The name and address of each incorporator must be included.

Capitalization: This is a list of the number and types of shares of stock the corporation will be authorized to issue. It is no longer necessary to assign a par value to shares.

Initial board: This is a list of names of people who will serve as board of directors members until the first shareholder meeting.

Registered agent: A registered agent is the person or entity designated to receive notice on behalf of a corporation when it is involved in a legal proceeding. The articles must list the name and address of the registered agent.
questions.explanationJa: 会社は、州の機関（州務長官など）に定款を提出し、受理されることで成立する。定款には一般に、名称、事業目的、存続期間、発起人、発行可能な株式の数と種類（資本構成）、当初の取締役、登録代理人の氏名と住所を記載する。登録代理人は、会社が訴訟に関わったときに会社に代わって通知を受ける者である。よって、登録代理人の氏名も発行可能株式数も定款に記載する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.6

questions.stem: Which of the following actions may a corporation's board of directors take without shareholder approval?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consolidation with one or more corporations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Merger with one or more corporations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voluntary dissolution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purchase of 55% of another corporation's stock.

questions.explanation:
Shareholders are the owners of a corporation, but they do not manage it. Instead, a corporation is managed by its board of directors (BOD) and corporate officers. Even though shareholders do not manage the corporation, they still have the right to vote on significant matters that affect the corporation, such as:

Election of BOD members

Dissolution of the corporation ("Voluntary dissolution.")

Mergers and consolidations ("Consolidation with one or more corporations." / "Merger with one or more corporations.")

Amendments to the articles of incorporation

Loans to directors

Liquidating dividends

Consolidations, mergers, and dissolutions are all fundamental changes in a corporation's structure. Purchasing another corporation's stock does not change the corporation's structure and therefore falls within the BOD function of establishing the corporation's strategic direction.

Note: A shareholder may also be a corporate officer or a BOD member, or both. However, when making strategic and operational decisions, that person acts in the capacity of a BOD member or officer, not a shareholder.
questions.explanationJa: 会社は取締役会と役員が経営し、株主は経営しない。ただし、解散、合併・新設合併、定款変更など会社の構造を根本的に変える事項には株主の承認が必要である。他社株式を55%取得することは会社自体の構造を変えるものではなく、会社の戦略方針を決める取締役会の権限に含まれるので、株主の承認なしに行える。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.7

questions.stem: Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following conditions is necessary for a corporation to achieve a successful voluntary dissolution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Successful application to the secretary of state in which the corporation holds its primary place of business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A recommendation of dissolution by the board of directors and approval by a majority of all shareholders entitled to vote.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approval by the board of directors of an amendment to the certificate of incorporation calling for the dissolution of the corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unanimous approval of the board of directors and all shareholders entitled to vote on a resolution of voluntary dissolution.

questions.explanation:
Even though shareholders do not manage the corporation, they still have the right to vote on significant matters affecting the corporation, such as:

Election of BOD members

Dissolution of the corporation

Mergers and consolidations

Amendments to the articles of incorporation

Loans to directors

Liquidating dividends

Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act (RMBCA), a corporation can voluntarily dissolve if there is a recommendation by the BOD to do so and that recommendation is approved by a majority of the shareholders entitled to vote. The RMBCA does not require unanimous approval of the BOD and the shareholders ("Unanimous approval of the board of directors and all shareholders ent…").

("Successful application to the secretary of state in which the corpora…") The RMBCA does not require application to or approval from the secretary of state to voluntarily dissolve a corporation.

("Approval by the board of directors of an amendment to the certificate…") The RMBCA does not require an amendment to the articles of incorporation in order to voluntarily dissolve the corporation.
questions.explanationJa: 改訂模範事業会社法（RMBCA）では、取締役会が解散を勧告し、議決権を持つ株主の過半数がそれを承認すれば、会社は任意解散できる。取締役会と株主の全員一致までは求められていない。州務長官への申請・承認や、解散のための定款変更も必要とされない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.8

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding a general partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partnership debt must be apportioned based on partnership percentages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partnership must file a certificate of formation with its home state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Partners have unlimited liability for partnership debts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The partnership must remit federal income taxes on behalf of the partners.

questions.explanation:
A general partnership is an association between two or more persons or entities to operate a business as co-owners for profit. A general partnership can be created formally (a written agreement) or informally (a rock band). In either case there is no requirement to file a certificate of formation with the partnership's home state ("The partnership must file a certificate of formation with its home st…"). Corporations, limited liability companies, and limited partnerships require a more formal process for creation (formation documents, state filing fees).

One difference between general partnerships and more formally created entities is that general partners have unlimited liability for partnership debt. In contrast, shareholders in a corporation are not personally liable for the corporation's debts.

("Partnership debt must be apportioned based on partnership percentages.") There are no absolute requirements for how partnership debt will be apportioned among the partners. Absent a contrary agreement among the partners, the debt will be apportioned in accordance with the partnership profit and loss percentages for each partner.

("The partnership must remit federal income taxes on behalf of the part…") For tax purposes, a partnership is considered a pass-through entity and neither pays income taxes nor remits taxes on behalf of the partners. Partners include their share of partnership income/loss and separately stated items on their own income tax returns.
questions.explanationJa: ジェネラル・パートナーは、パートナーシップの債務に無限責任を負う。これは、会社の株主が会社の債務について個人的責任を負わないのと対照的である。ジェネラル・パートナーシップは書面でも非公式にでも成立し、州に設立証明書を提出する必要はない。債務の負担割合に絶対的な決まりはなく、別段の合意がなければ損益分配割合による。また、パススルー事業体なので、パートナーに代わって連邦所得税を納めることもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.9

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of forming a limited liability company (LLC) as opposed to a partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The entity may avoid taxation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entity may have multiple owners.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The owners may participate in management while limiting personal liability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The owners may receive allocations and distributions disproportionately.

questions.explanation:
Limited liability companies (LLCs) are hybrid entities that have characteristics of both partnerships and corporations. From a tax standpoint, an LLC can elect to be a pass-through entity (and therefore not be subject to income tax) and be treated like a partnership ("The entity may avoid taxation.").

From a legal standpoint, LLCs provide all owners (members) with the limited liability protection of a corporation. This applies even to members who actively participate in the LLC's business. Limited liability for all owners is an advantage of an LLC as opposed to a partnership, in which some or all owners have unlimited liability.

In a general partnership, all partners are general partners who have unlimited liability for the partnership's debts. In a limited partnership, the limited partners have limited liability, just like members in an LLC. However, a limited partnership is required to have at least one general partner who has unlimited personal liability for the partnership's debts.

("The entity may have multiple owners.") Both partnerships and LLCs can have multiple owners. In fact, by definition, partnerships are required to have at least two owners.

("The owners may receive allocations and distributions disproportionate…") Disproportionate allocations and distributions are allowed in partnerships and LLCs.
questions.explanationJa: LLCはパートナーシップと会社の性質を併せ持ち、経営に積極的に参加するメンバーも含めて、全メンバーが会社と同様の有限責任を受ける。これがパートナーシップに対するLLCの利点である。ジェネラル・パートナーシップでは全員が無限責任を負い、LPでも少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーは無限責任を負う。課税を避けられること（パススルー課税）、複数のオーナーを持てること、不均等な配分・分配ができることは、パートナーシップとLLCの両方に当てはまるので、LLCだけの利点ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.10

questions.stem: The corporate veil is most likely to be pierced and the shareholders held personally liable if

choices.label: A
choices.text: The corporation has elected S corporation status under the Internal Revenue Code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The shareholders have commingled their personal funds with those of the corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An ultra vires act has been committed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A partnership incorporates its business solely to limit the liability of its partners.

questions.explanation:
One of the primary reasons to form a corporation is to limit the owners' personal liability while operating a business ("A partnership incorporates its business solely to limit the liability…"). This protection is often referred to as a corporate veil because it shields shareholders' personal assets from being used to satisfy the corporation's liabilities. However, courts can pierce the corporate veil and hold shareholders personally liable for the corporation's liabilities in these circumstances:

Undercapitalization: This occurs if the capital the shareholders contributed to form the corporation is inadequate to meet the corporation's reasonable financial needs.

Shareholder fraud: In this situation, shareholders create a corporation with the intent to commit fraud (Ponzi scheme). This is not to be confused with ultra vires acts (unauthorized acts) by directors and officers, which do not result in shareholder liability ("An ultra vires act has been committed.").

Ignoring corporate formalities: This occurs when shareholders operate the corporation without following legal formalities, such as electing a board of directors and holding shareholder and board meetings. In essence, the shareholders act as if the corporation does not exist.

Commingling assets: In this situation, shareholders consistently treat corporate assets as if they were the shareholders' personal assets, using them for personal purposes (paying a home mortgage).

("The corporation has elected S corporation status under the Internal R…") Electing S corporation status is a decision as to how the entity will be taxed. It would not lead to the corporation's veil being pierced.
questions.explanationJa: 会社の法人格（コーポレート・ベール）は、株主の個人財産を会社の債務から守る。ただし、過少資本、詐欺目的の設立、会社の形式（取締役の選任や会議の開催）の無視、資産の混同がある場合は、裁判所が法人格を否認して株主に個人責任を負わせることがある。株主が個人資金と会社資金を混同していれば、法人格否認の典型例に当たる。有限責任を得ることだけを目的とする法人化は正当であり、S法人の選択は課税方法の選択にすぎない。取締役・役員の越権行為（ultra vires）も、株主の責任にはつながらない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.11

questions.stem: Which of the following parties is required to repay an illegal distribution made by a corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distribution from a solvent corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distribution from an insolvent corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from a solvent corporation was illegal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from an insolvent corporation was illegal.

questions.explanation:
A corporation's board of directors (BOD) determines if and when dividends will be declared and paid to shareholders. Until declaration, the corporation has no liability to the shareholders.

In general, state corporate law prohibits the BOD from declaring a dividend if the corporation is insolvent or if the dividend will render it insolvent. If the corporation is solvent, the BOD may declare any dividend amount up to the higher of the company's retained earnings or current period earnings ("A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distr…").

If the BOD wants to declare a dividend that exceeds these amounts, the shareholders must approve the portion that is a return of capital (a liquidating distribution). A dividend distribution that contains a return of capital and is not approved by the shareholders is considered an illegal distribution.

If a corporation pays an illegal dividend, a shareholder may keep it if the shareholder was unaware that it was illegal and if the corporation was solvent ("A shareholder who did not know a distribution received from a solvent…"). Shareholders must repay an illegal distribution they received from an insolvent corporation regardless of whether they knew the distribution was illegal.

("A director who did not breach a fiduciary duty when approving a distr…") A director who declares a dividend when the corporation is or would be rendered insolvent is in breach of a fiduciary duty. However, if the director takes this action based on incorrect information provided by management, the director is not in breach of a fiduciary duty and is not required to repay the illegal dividend.
questions.explanationJa: 州の会社法は、会社が支払不能の場合、または配当によって支払不能になる場合に、取締役会が配当を宣言することを禁じている。違法な配当を受け取った株主は、違法と知らず、かつ会社に支払能力があれば、受け取った配当を保持できる。しかし、支払不能の会社から受け取った違法な分配は、違法と知っていたかどうかにかかわらず返還しなければならない。経営者から誤った情報を受けて宣言した取締役のように、受託者責任に違反していない取締役は返還義務を負わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.12

questions.stem: Under the Revised Model Business Corporation Act, which of the following statements is correct regarding corporate officers of a public corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An officer may not simultaneously serve as a director.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A corporation may be authorized to indemnify its officers for liability incurred in a suit by stockholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stockholders always have the right to elect a corporation's officers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An officer of a corporation is required to own at least one share of the corporation's stock.

questions.explanation:
Corporation officers have a fiduciary duty to the corporation and stockholders (ie, owners). This fiduciary responsibility means that the officers must act with a duty of care (honestly, prudently) and with a duty of loyalty. If they honor these duties, then, according to the business judgment rule, they will not be held liable for their good faith errors in judgment.

However, shareholders and other parties may file lawsuits against the corporation and its officers for breach of fiduciary duties of care and loyalty. Accordingly, a corporation's board of directors (BOD) may vote to indemnify (reimburse) officers who are found to be personally liable in a shareholder lawsuit. The BOD must believe that the indemnity is in the best interest of the company. In addition, the indemnity must not be a violation of public policy (indemnification for engaging in illegal activity).

("An officer may not simultaneously serve as a director.") It is common practice for officers to serve on the BOD.

("Stockholders always have the right to elect a corporation's officers.") The shareholders elect the BOD. The BOD then elects the officers.

("An officer of a corporation is required to own at least one share of…") Officers may own shares in the company they manage; however, it is not mandatory.
questions.explanationJa: 役員は会社と株主に対して注意義務と忠実義務を負い、これを守っていれば、経営判断の原則により誠実な判断の誤りについて責任を問われない。ただし、株主などから受託者責任違反で訴えられることはある。その場合、取締役会は、会社の最善の利益になり公序に反しない（違法行為の補償ではない）と判断すれば、株主代表訴訟などで個人責任を負った役員を補償できる。役員が取締役を兼ねることは一般的であり、役員を選任するのは株主ではなく取締役会であり、役員が株式を保有する義務もない。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is a general requirement for the merger of two corporations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the stockholders of both corporations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the boards of both corporations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The absorbed corporation must amend its articles of incorporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The stockholders of both corporations must be given due notice of a special meeting, including a copy or summary of the merger plan.

questions.explanation:
General legal requirements for corporate mergers and consolidations

Corporate approval

Majority of members on board of directors of each corporation must approve

Call special shareholder meetings and provide copy of plan

Majority of shareholders of each corporation must approve*

Government approval

File the approved plan with state authorities

State authorities issue certificate of approval

Dissenting shareholders

Dissenting shareholders have right to have their shares appraised and purchased at that price

Short-form mergers (90%-owned subsidiary into a parent) generally do not require shareholder approval.

one legal requirement is that stockholders of both corporations must be given due notice of a special meeting to approve the merger. They must also be provided with a copy or summary of the merger plan. This process ensures that shareholders receive both sufficient notice of the merger and the information they need to make an informed decision.

("The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the stockholders of b…" / "The merger plan must be approved unanimously by the boards of both co…") Mergers and consolidations require approval by a majority, not the unanimous approval, of both the board of directors and shareholders of each corporation.

("The absorbed corporation must amend its articles of incorporation.") When two corporations merge, one (surviving corporation) absorbs all the assets and liabilities of the other (merged corporation). After the merger, the merged (absorbed) corporation no longer exists, and therefore its articles of incorporation are no longer valid.
questions.explanationJa: 合併には、各会社の取締役会の過半数の承認と、株主総会での株主の過半数の承認が必要である（全員一致ではない）。その前提として、両社の株主に臨時株主総会の適切な通知を行い、合併計画の写しまたは要約を提供しなければならない。これにより、株主は十分な情報に基づいて判断できる。吸収される会社は合併後に消滅するので、その定款を変更する必要はない。

questions.stem: Which of the following types of business entities permits all of its owners to manage the entity and have limited liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Joint venture.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limited liability partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited liability company.

questions.explanation:
Limited liability companies (LLCs) are hybrid entities that have characteristics of both partnerships and corporations. From a legal standpoint, LLCs provide all owners (members) with the limited liability protection equal to that of a corporation. Basically, an LLC's owners (members) are not personally liable for the debts and obligations of the LLC, similar to shareholders in a corporation. This applies even to members who actively participate in the LLC's business.

A limited liability partnership (LLP) has characteristics of partnerships and corporations. The difference is that in an LLP, a partner has unlimited personal liability for the LLP's liabilities created by that partner's own torts (negligence) ("Limited liability partnership.").

("Joint venture.") Joint ventures share many characteristics with general partnerships, such as unlimited liability that is joint and several for all parties who participate in the joint venture.

("Limited partnership.") In a limited partnership (LP), only limited partners have limited liability. An LP must have at least one general partner, and that person has unlimited liability. In addition, a limited partner who actively manages the LP will be considered a general partner and lose limited liability protection.
questions.explanationJa: LLCでは、経営に積極的に参加するメンバーも含めて、全メンバーが会社の株主と同様の有限責任を受けるので、全オーナーが経営に参加しつつ有限責任を得られる。LLPでは、パートナーは自分自身の不法行為（過失など）による債務について無限責任を負う。ジョイント・ベンチャーはジェネラル・パートナーシップと同じく参加者全員が連帯無限責任を負う。LPでは少なくとも1人のジェネラル・パートナーが無限責任を負い、経営に参加したリミテッド・パートナーは有限責任を失う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.15

questions.stem: Which of the following partners of a limited liability partnership (LLP) may avoid personal liability when a partner commits a negligent act?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All the partners

choices.label: B
choices.text: The supervisor of the negligent partner

choices.label: C
choices.text: All the partners other than the negligent partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: All the partners other than the supervisor of and the negligent partner

questions.explanation:
A limited liability partnership (LLP) is a type of legal entity that provides some or all of its owners with limited liability. It is like a general partnership; all partners have the right to participate in management of the partnership. LLPs are popular among professionals (CPAs, lawyers) because they provide partners with liability protection from other partners' torts (negligence, malpractice) ("All the partners" / "All the partners other than the negligent partner").

Generally, partners in an LLP are personally liable for their own torts. In addition, supervising partners (a managing partner) are liable for the torts of those they supervise ("The supervisor of the negligent partner"). However, the other partners in the LLP avoid liability for torts committed by other partners.

For example, if a CPA partner in an LLP negligently performs an audit, that CPA is liable for the damages suffered by those harmed by the negligence. If that CPA was supervised by another partner in the firm (the managing partner), that supervising partner is also personally liable for the negligence. However, other partner CPAs in the firm are not personally liable.
questions.explanationJa: LLPは、他のパートナーの不法行為（過失や職務上の過誤）についての責任からパートナーを守るため、CPAや弁護士に好まれる。ただし、パートナーは自分自身の不法行為について個人責任を負い、監督するパートナー（マネージング・パートナーなど）も、監督下の者の不法行為について責任を負う。したがって、個人責任を免れるのは、過失を犯したパートナーとその監督者を除く、その他のパートナーである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Business structure Q.16
